jobs.title: Community Health Worker - Medicaid
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Community Health Worker - Medicaid based in the United States.

This role serves as a trusted connection between Medicaid members, healthcare providers, community organizations, and care management teams.

You will work directly with members to improve health literacy, address barriers to care, and connect people with valuable community resources.

The position combines face-to-face and telephone outreach with education, advocacy, care coordination, and social needs support.

You will focus on helping members close care gaps, access preventive services, and take a more active role in their health and wellness.

The role also provides an opportunity to build strong partnerships with community organizations serving vulnerable and at-risk populations.

You will work independently while collaborating closely with internal care management teams and external providers.

This is a purpose-driven opportunity for an empathetic, culturally aware professional who wants to make a measurable difference in the lives of Medicaid members.

Accountabilities

Conduct face-to-face and telephone outreach to Medicaid members around preventive health, care gaps, maternity, care transitions, health-related social needs, and chronic condition initiatives.
Educate members on the importance of preventive healthcare services, assess opportunities for additional care management support, and make appropriate referrals to internal programs and community resources.
Coordinate with members, healthcare providers, and community organizations to help individuals access preventive services and address health-related social needs.
Build trusting relationships with members and empower them to take an active role in managing their health, wellness, and healthcare decisions.
Develop partnerships with community-based organizations and human services providers, including programs such as Head Start, WIC, community centers, and homeless shelters, to identify and engage members who may need additional support.
Conduct Social Determinants of Health assessments when appropriate and help members address barriers such as transportation, childcare, financial challenges, limited healthcare knowledge, and difficulty navigating the healthcare system.
Assist members with scheduling appointments, answering healthcare-related questions, and connecting them with appropriate services and resources.
Develop and contribute to educational materials for members and providers and communicate outreach results, outcomes, and community education activities to management and colleagues.
Participate in developing measurable and innovative programs designed to reach and support at-risk member populations.
Maintain current knowledge of available health plan benefits and lines of business to ensure members receive accurate and relevant information.
Represent the organization at community events and activities hosted by community partners.
Collaborate closely with care management and other internal teams to refer members for additional education, support, and services outside the role’s scope.

Requirements

Have at least 1 year of experience in a healthcare-related customer service, outreach, or marketing environment demonstrating the ability to engage members and encourage participation in health or care management programs.
Have at least 1 year of experience as a Community Health Worker or in a closely related field.
Hold a High School diploma or GED.
Obtain Certified Community Health Worker (CCHW) certification through the Pennsylvania Certification Board within 12 months of the start date.
Demonstrate knowledge of customer service principles, including understanding customer needs and maintaining appropriate quality standards.
Communicate effectively with members, peers, supervisors, providers, and community partners while contributing positively as part of a team.
Demonstrate independent and creative problem-solving skills, with the ability to be proactive, self-directed, assertive, and resourceful.
Be able to manage multiple priorities simultaneously and respond promptly and professionally to member needs and concerns.
Possess strong written and verbal communication skills, along with patience, empathy, and a member-focused approach.
Demonstrate cultural awareness and sensitivity when working with Medicaid populations, including individuals with limited English proficiency and diverse social and cultural backgrounds.
Understand common healthcare access barriers, including transportation, childcare, limited preventive-health knowledge, distrust of healthcare systems, and personal, social, or financial challenges.
Demonstrate the ability to work independently in the community while maintaining strong collaboration with internal and external stakeholders.
Basic medical terminology knowledge is preferred.
Experience working directly with the targeted community or population is preferred.
Be prepared to travel approximately 50%–75% as required by the role.

Benefits

Competitive base pay ranging from $20.72 to $30.12 per hour, depending on qualifications, experience, expected contributions, internal equity, market factors, and business considerations.
Remote or office-based working options, with no requirement for a physical work site.
Opportunity to make a direct impact on Medicaid member health outcomes, wellness, and access to care.
Purpose-driven work focused on health education, care-gap closure, social needs, and community support.
Meaningful collaboration with healthcare providers, community organizations, care management professionals, and other internal teams.
Opportunity to build relationships with community partners and develop practical expertise in population health and healthcare navigation.
Supportive environment that values cultural competency, empathy, teamwork, and member advocacy.
Opportunities to contribute to innovative programs designed to better reach and support at-risk populations.

PURPOSE AND SCOPE:

The Care Navigation MSW promotes ongoing care coordination problem solving and customer support resulting in quality patient care for Fresenius Health Partners (FHP) Care Navigation population by providing guidance, support, and other care coordination functions as defined by the pertinent program. The Care Navigation MSW monitors and intervenes with FHP patients who are at high risk of poor health outcomes, have poor adherence to recommended treatments and/or have complex psychosocial barriers. The Care Navigation Unit MSW provides psychosocial services to patients managed by Fresenius Health Partners utilizing Social Work Theory of Human Behavior and accepted methods of social work practice. The Care Navigation Unit MSW works with the health care team to promote positive adjustment, rehabilitation and improved quality of life for patients. In collaboration with the interdisciplinary team, informs, educates and supports staff in understanding the emotional, psychological and behavioral impact of Chronic Kidney Disease on the patient and family to ensure comprehensive quality care of our patients. Services are generally provided telephonically but there may be programs where on site visits to clinics, medical offices, hospitals and/or patient homes are required. Programs principally include the Care Navigation Unit but could extend to other Company care management programs. Maintains a database of all interactions and supports a positive rapport with our patients, affiliated providers and vendors.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Responsible for driving the FMCNA culture through values and customer service standards.
Accountable for outstanding customer service to all external and internal customers.
Develops and maintains effective relationships through effective and timely communication.
Takes initiative and action to respond, resolve and follow up regarding customer service issues with all customers in a timely manner.
Using defined trigger events initiated outbound communication to patient/family caregivers and/or other concerned parties facilitate the coordination of care for patients assigned to the Care Navigation unit.
Receives referrals from Care Navigation Unit staff, patients/families or dialysis clinic staff regarding patients at high risk of poor health outcomes, non-adherent to treatment recommendations and/or with complex psychosocial barriers. Identifies root cause(s) of barrier(s), develops plan of intervention, executes intervention with team members and monitors success of intervention. Re-evaluates interventions and plan as necessary.
Utilizes established social work theory and methods and quality of life measurement instruments as part of assessment and care planning to resolve barriers and meet patient treatment goals.
Provides established outcomes driven psycho-educational counseling methods aimed at improving areas of need, treatment adherence, vocational/educational rehabilitation and/or quality of life.
Provides ongoing education to patient/family regarding psychosocial issues related to End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) and all support services that are available.
Collaborates with clinical staff and other members of the patient's health care team to assist in the development of an individual plan of care to facilitate an immediate action plan to meet the patient's current needs.
Communicates and coordinates with patient, appropriate members of patient's health care team (i.e. Nephrologist office, Primary Care office, hospital, etc.) in developing, executing and reviewing results of care coordination efforts (closing the loop).
Social service and community resource navigation and referral, including emergency food, housing, shelter or transportation resources.
Identify appropriate community social service agencies and other resources to assist patient and families. This may include, but is not limited to assisting patient in securing financial assistance, obtaining medical transportation, identifying mental health treatment and any other public and private resources deemed necessary.
Assists clinics to identify and manage interventions for patients that are at risk of poor health outcomes.
Collects, reviews and employs all pertinent information available from but not limited to FMC clinical systems, care management notes, vendor information, geographic mapping software, direct communication patient, physician or other members of health care team.
Reports to clinical staff, the discovery of unreported medical or social conditions or changes at home that may lead to adverse outcomes and ensures that these are referred to appropriate sources for attention.
Maintains and updates the appropriate software/tracking logs of patients in the Care Navigation Program to manage and record required information and data.
Evaluates program processes and makes recommendations to management that will improve the effectiveness and efficiency of the program.

Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. Job Summary

The Program Manager for Faculty Training & Enrichment is responsible for supporting the planning, coordination, implementation, and evaluation of faculty and trainee training and enrichment initiatives across the AMC Department of Medicine. Working under the direction of the Senior Director of Faculty Affairs, this position partners closely with the Vice Chair for Faculty & Trainee Enrichment and other department leaders to coordinate faculty training and enrichment programming, mentoring initiatives, educational events, communications, and operational projects that enhance faculty engagement, professional growth, and career advancement.

In addition, the Program Manager provides Faculty Affairs support for assigned clinical divisions and departmental initiatives, including academic writing and faculty promotion activities, and serves as the departmental administrator for the Online Letter Request Portal (OLRP), ensuring the efficient coordination and tracking of external referee letters and promotion workflows. The position also supports administrative and operational functions that advance the strategic priorities of the AMC Department of Medicine.

Qualifications

Faculty Training & Enrichment

Coordinate and support faculty and trainee training and enrichment initiatives in partnership with the Vice Chair for Faculty & Trainee Enrichment. Assist with the planning, implementation, and evaluation of mentoring programs, faculty training and enrichment activities, workshops, seminars, and educational programming. Develop meeting materials, presentations, communications, reports, agendas, and other resources to support faculty training and enrichment initiatives. Coordinate faculty engagement activities, networking events, recognition programs, and special initiatives that foster an inclusive, collaborative, and enriching faculty environment. Monitor program participation, outcomes, and performance metrics, and prepare reports for department leadership. Partner with faculty, division administrators, and department leadership throughout the appointments and promotions process. Support faculty appointments, reappointments, promotion process, and other strategic Faculty Affairs projects as assigned.

Online Letter Request Portal (OLRP) Administration

Monitor promotion timelines and ensure timely completion of OLRP milestones. Provide training and support to faculty, division administrators, and reviewers utilizing the OLRP. Develop reports, maintain system documentation, monitor portal activity, and recommend workflow improvements. Collaborate with Faculty Affairs leadership and technical partners to enhance portal functionality and operational efficiency.

Prepare presentations, newsletters, website content, reports, and departmental communications. Maintain program records, databases, and documentation while ensuring confidentiality and data integrity. A Brief Overview

The Social Worker (MSW) is responsible for supporting safe, timely, and effective patient transitions throughout the acute care episode. This role focuses on psychosocial assessment, discharge planning, resource coordination, and patient/family support. Documentation & Compliance Completes timely and accurate documentation in the electronic medical record. Adheres to CMS, Joint Commission, and hospital policies related to discharge planning and patient rights. Supports hospital initiatives such as readmission reduction, length-of-stay management, and value-based care models (e.g., TEAM Model)

This position does not: Provide psychotherapy or clinical counseling Diagnose mental health conditions Conduct clinical risk assessments requiring licensure Perform clinical interventions reserved for licensed providers

Required - Master's Degree Social Work

Experience in acute care, healthcare, social services or community resource coordination preferred.
Knowledge of discharge planning, community resources, and healthcare systems strongly preferred.

Preferred - Licensed Master Social Worker Mississippi - Mississippi Board of Examiners for Social Workers

Excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability to work collaboratively and cooperatively within an integrated interdisciplinary team.

Ability to gather, synthesize, and summarize relevant data to support sound judgment and patient-centered clinical decision-making.
Strong oral and written communication skills, enabling effective, professional interaction with hospital staff, agency partners, health care professionals, patients, and families.

Organizational skills to manage multiple tasks, caseloads, and projects while maintaining accuracy and workflow control.
Ability to use initiative and exercise independent judgment, with well developed critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
Demonstrated ability to develop and maintain effective working relationships with physicians and collaborate with health care professionals at all levels to achieve shared goals.

Exposure to patient body fluids as well as exposure to hazardous or poisonous materials.

The role also provides an opportunity to build strong partnerships with community organizations serving vulnerable and at-risk populations.

Conducts interviews, assessments, and evaluations of patients and family members to identify social, emotional, and economic factors which may interfere with obtaining maximum benefits from medical care.

Since 1944, Boys & Girls Clubs of Central Florida has provided children and teens, ages 6 to 18, with a safe place to learn and grow during non-school hours. The mission of Boys & Girls Clubs of Central Florida is to inspire and enable all young people, especially those who need us most, to realize their full potential as productive, responsible, and caring adults. Every day after school and all summer long, our members walk through the blue doors at little or no cost to their families and find academic support, enrichment, and caring adult role models who believe in what they can become.

How we do it matters as much as what we do. Our Clubs deliver quality programming grounded in evidence across six core pillars of focus: education and career development; character and leadership development; sports, fitness, and recreation; health and life skills; the arts; and mental health. That work is reinforced by practices informed by trauma research, mental and emotional wellness support, and an unwavering commitment to safety. The results show up in graduation rates, college and vocational school enrollment, grades, and young people who tell us they feel emotionally safe at their Club. As part of the national Future Ready movement, we are growing bigger, better, and bolder, and we know none of it happens without exceptional people. That is why we invest in our team through comprehensive training, leader development, competitive compensation and benefits, and a workplace culture built on excellence, belonging, and accountability. Administration And Reporting

& COMPETENCIES
